page_title: MagicInput | One Keyboard and Mouse for Your Mac and PC

sources.entry: MagicInput - Share one keyboard and mouse between a Mac and a Windows PC by moving the pointer past the screen edge, with clipboard sync and file transfer. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: MagicInput
summary.one_liner: MagicInput shares one keyboard and mouse between a Mac and a Windows PC by letting the pointer cross the screen edge, with copy/paste sync.
keywords: copy paste between mac and pc
use one keyboard for two computers
use_cases: Using one keyboard and mouse across a Mac and a Windows PC
Copying and pasting text between a Mac and a PC
Controlling a PC from a Mac trackpad on a shared desk
Arranging a Windows PC beside Mac displays or an iPad via Sidecar
summary.what_it_does: MagicInput lets the pointer move off one screen and continue on the other computer, so typing, clicking, scrolling and dragging work across a Mac and a Windows PC. Keyboard input follows whichever computer the user last clicked into. Copied text is shared between the machines, and Command and Ctrl are swapped automatically so shortcuts work. Screen layout is set up by dragging the PC beside the Mac's displays, and an iPad can be included as a Sidecar display. The page says all traffic is encrypted, stays on the local network, and that the source code is public on GitHub.
notable: Pointer crosses between screens; keyboard follows the last click
Source code published on GitHub; release checksums and Apple-notarized Mac app
No account, cloud or telemetry; works only on the local network
Installable on Mac via Homebrew cask
caveats: Business use requires a paid license: $10 monthly, $96 yearly or $199 lifetime
Requires macOS 13+ and Windows 10 or 11 on the same local network
Page does not clearly say whether the Windows side is a separate install or whether file transfer is included in the free tier
